page: Amazon Web Services z1d.2xlarge is a high-frequency, memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8151 processor configured with 4 dedicated physical cores, 8 vCPUs via hyper-threading, and a sustained base clock frequency of 4.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a shared 24 MB L3 cache, with instruction support for AVX and AVX-512F. Hardware resources feature 64.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Storage comprises a bundled 300 GB local NVMe SSD, and the network interface provides a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth. No physical GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent performance across core-sensitive and memory-bound metrics. The instance recorded 1,320.0 in Geekbench single-core, 5,016.0 in multi-core testing, and 8,155.0 in Clang compilation. Memory throughput tests registered 52.49 GB/sec read and 38.08 GB/sec write on large 256 MB blocks, while in-memory operations reached 8.47 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, performance metrics dip under heavily parallel tasks; multi-threaded bzip3 decompression settled in the lower 25% bracket at 32.15 GB/sec, and medium 7B model LLM prompt processing reached 13.21 tokens per second due to the 4-physical-core ceiling and absence of specialized matrix instruction extensions such as AMX or AVX-512 VNNI.

The qualitative efficiency profile of the z1d.2xlarge favors environments that require high single-thread clock rates paired with generous memory allocations and low-latency local scratch storage. Deploying this instance yields high utilization for workloads constrained by per-core software licensing or linear transaction paths. Primary operational fits include relational databases, Redis caching layers, electronic design automation (EDA), continuous integration build nodes, and high-throughput web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services z1d.2xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by an Intel Xeon 8151 processor offering a sustained core frequency of 4.0 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro system with x86_64 architecture, it provisions 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs alongside 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Dedicated hardware includes 300 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a 2 Gbps baseline network interface, while accelerators like GPUs are omitted. Benchmark metrics reflect consistent mid-tier results across general compute and memory throughput tests, achieving 8.47 million Redis SET operations per second and 3,210.87 operations in PassMark database testing. However, parallel workloads such as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and larger 7B language model execution exhibit lower relative throughput due to the 4-core boundary. The instance is suited for relational databases, electronic design automation, in-memory caches, and high-frequency per-core enterprise applications.
